themes_detail.label: Street Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor Enforcement complaints spiked to 9 this week, a 454% increase over the 1.6-per-week baseline (z-score: 6.05), suggesting either a sudden crackdown or emerging vendor activity that residents perceive as problematic in Belmont/East Tremont.
evidence: 9 Vendor Enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 6.05 indicates statistically significant spike (high severity)
Timing suggests either new enforcement action by city or new vendor activity/clustering
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY/DOH about any new enforcement sweeps in the district this week
Canvass street vendors, bodega owners, and residents about what triggered the spike—pushcart density, food carts, unlicensed sales?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Parking Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Illegal Parking complaints jumped to 124 last week, a 68% spike above the 73.6-per-week baseline (z-score: 3.93), indicating a possible recent change in enforcement, parking supply, or resident tolerance in the district.
evidence: 124 Illegal Parking complaints last week vs. 73.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Illegal Parking is already the 3rd-largest complaint category (1,018 total in 90 days), now accelerating
reporting_angles: Check NYPD/DOT parking enforcement ticket data to see if citation volume also spiked last week
Interview residents on specific blocks to understand if parking availability or double-parkers are worsening

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street/Sidewalk Noise complaints surged to 89 two weeks ago, a 225% increase above the 27.4-per-week baseline (z-score: 4.08), reflecting a significant spike in complaints about outdoor noise, construction, or street activity in the district.
evidence: 89 Street/Sidewalk Noise complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 27.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Street/Sidewalk Noise ranks 8th in overall 90-day complaint volume (418 total), but spike is recent and acute
reporting_angles: Canvass residents to identify specific noise sources: construction, street vendors, traffic, bars, or events
Cross-reference with DOB permits and Department of Environmental Protection noise complaint logs to pinpoint source

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead Animal complaints skyrocketed to 10 three weeks ago, a 900% spike above the 1.0-per-week baseline (z-score: 9.0, highest on spike list), suggesting a possible pest infestation, animal welfare, or sanitation emergency in specific locations.
evidence: 10 Dead Animal complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 9.0 (highest severity of all spikes on this report)
Aligns with 300% spike in Residential Disposal Complaints (4 complaints same week vs. 1.0 avg), suggesting broader waste/sanitation issue
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY and NYC Parks about dead animals found and cause of death—rodents, stray dogs, disease?
Investigate whether spike correlates to waste management problems, restaurant closures, or pest control failures in specific blocks

themes_detail.label: Park Rules Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Violation of Park Rules complaints jumped to 3 two weeks ago, a 1100% spike above the 0.2-per-week baseline (z-score: 6.35), indicating emerging issues with park usage, enforcement gaps, or specific disruptive activity at Belmont/East Tremont parks.
evidence: 3 Park Rules Violation complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Aligns with long-standing community board budget requests for park upgrades/amenities, suggesting under-resourced parks
reporting_angles: Identify which parks saw violations—Crotona Park, Joyce Kilmer Park, or others—and what specific rules were broken
Interview Parks enforcement and residents to determine if violations are related to inadequate facilities, security, or maintenance
